about: MIT-China presents the China Diaologue Series. Panelists Professors Xiaoxing Xi and Gang Chen, moderated by Professor Yasheng Huang, will explore how professional achievement can intersect with heightened national-security considerations. Drawing on personal experiences and institutional perspectives, the discussion will address evolving policies and the broader implications for academia, scientific research, and international collaboration.

events.title: SURGE: A Participatory Performance on Sea Level Rise
about: Experience sea level rise through this interactive performance-workshop that combines movement, climate science, and activism at the MIT Museum.

Choreographer Jessie Jeanne Stinnett and Boston Dance Theater Core Members will lead a 45-minute participatory workshop. Through guided movement and collective exploration, you'll engage with sea level rise impacts—ocean warming, ice melt, tidal dynamics, and shifting coastlines—and contribute your own perspectives as the workshop builds toward imagining possible futures. No dance experience is needed.
A 30-minute performance follows, where audiences mingle with performers to witness, reflect, and dialogue about climate science and coastal change.
SURGE creates an accessible space for curiosity, conversation, and collective understanding of climate challenges, where science, art, and community voices intersect.
We have a limited number of free tickets available for full-time students with ID. Please reach out to museumregadmin@mit.edu.
This program is presented as part of the MIT Museum’s thematic focus on OCEANS.

events.title: Author Ted Chiang in Conversation with MIT President Sally Kornbluth
about: Join us for a special conversation with author Ted Chiang and MIT President Sally Kornbluth about Exhalation. President Kornbluth has chosen Chiang’s celebrated science fiction short story collection to celebrate 10 years of MIT Reads. Exploring the book’s provocative questions about technology and humanity, their discussion will focus on the stories "The Truth of Fact, the Truth of Feeling,” "The Lifecycle of Software Objects,” “Omphalos,” “What’s Expected of Us," and "Exhalation."

In this fantastical and elegant collection, Chiang wrestles with the oldest questions on Earth – What is the nature of the universe? What does it mean to be human? – and ones that no one else has even imagined. And, each in its own way, the stories prove that complex and thoughtful science fiction can rise to new heights of beauty, meaning, and compassion.

This event is part of MIT Reads, a program that embraces the power of reading and storytelling to cultivate social connection, individual reflection, and a sense of our shared humanity. Designed to foster empathy, curiosity, and belonging, MIT Reads brings together the campus community – and readers everywhere – through common reading experiences, author talks, and group discussions.
This hybrid event is free and open to all, but pre-registration is required. For online participants, the URL will be emailed closer to the event.

events.title: AI and the Future of Filmmaking
about: W97-160 · December 3 · Lecture and Discussion – 6-7.30p

AI and the Future of Filmmaking What works, what doesn't, and what comes next AI can now generate convincing video from a sentence. But can a filmmaker actually direct it? William Cusick, filmmaker and former Creative Director at Stability AI, has been making films with generative AI and building tools for it since the launch of Stable Diffusion in 2022. In this talk he shows what AI filmmaking can do today, where it breaks down, and what it changes about cameras, sets, actors, and the director's job. He places the moment in a century of film technology, then looks ahead to real-time AI worlds where a film is generated while you watch it.
45-minute talk followed by discussion.
RSVP please. Open to all; no technical background needed.

William Cusick is a New York filmmaker and creative technologist who specializes in AI filmmaking. He was Creative Director at Stability AI during the public launch of Stable Diffusion and DreamStudio, and he is building Moviengine, an experimental system that turns screenplays into AI-generated films. He has directed two feature films, including Welcome to Nowhere (Bullet Hole Road) and Pop Meets the Void, designed projections for Broadway and international stage productions, and has taught at The New School for more than thirteen years.

events.title: Meriem Chabani. Communion It is embarrassing to believe. It is terrifying to care. What happens when we dare anyway?
about: Algerian born, Paris based Meriem Chabani is the founder and Principal of NEW SOUTH, an award-winning architecture, urban planning and anthropology practice that puts the margin at the center. Her work on civic spaces, memory and belonging includes includes the Taungdwingyi cultural center in Myanmar, the Globe Aroma refugee art center in Brussels, and the upcoming Mosque Zero in Paris. She is currently a finalist for the National Slavery Museum in Amsterdam. As an educator, Chabani has taught and lectured extensively. She has notably served as Aga Khan Design Critic in Architecture at Harvard GSD (USA), and currently teaches at Ecole Paris Malaquais (FR). Her work has regularly been distinguished and showcased at a number of international architecture Biennials, including Venice, Istanbul, Oslo and Lagos. In 2020 Chabani won the Europe 40 under 40 award from The European Centre for Architecture and The Chicago Athenaeum. In 2023, she is one of the emerging women architects for AMC. In 2025, Le Monde names her one of the leading voices in culture in France.

Sacred practices are often confined to religion, yet they can also be read as technologies of togetherness, ways of gathering bodies, knowledge, and memory into forms of collective action that outlast the institutions built to contain them.

Drawing on recent work by NEW SOUTH, this lecture explores how rituals, communal practices, and sacred spaces may shape architecture. From shared acts of making and gathering to spaces shaped by migration, displacement, and diasporic memory, these projects ask how architecture can support forms of solidarity that aren't always visible or formally recognized. Ritual here is also a spatial claim, a way of reoccupying ground for those pushed to the margins, relegated out of the mainstream, and denied formal recognition.

The lecture will explore how rituals rooted in care for land and its resources may offer a different model for building — one grounded in reciprocity rather than extraction. Architecture becomes less an object that organizes people than a framework through which people organize themselves. We may yet belong. We may yet forge futures not built on depletion.
Photo: Religious and Cultural Center in central Paris

events.title: New South—Meriem Chabani
about: Part of the MIT Fall 2026 Architecture Lecture Series.

Presented with The Aga Khan Program for Islamic Architecture Meriem has ten years of experience in complex territorial, urban, and architectural projects, with an emphasis on contexts that face significant socio-economic challenges, and a methodology that fosters dialogue and negotiation, federating diverse actors into multidisciplinary project leadership teams. As an educator, Meriem has taught and lectured extensively, shaping and currently teaching the Masters design studio ‘Afterlives’ at the Royal College of Arts (UK), and the African Health architecture studio at the École Nationale Supérieure d’Architecture Paris Malaquais (FR). In 2024, she was a Wheelwright Prize finalist.

This lecture will be held in person in the Sidara Auditorium (W41- 1216) and recorded. It will be available on YouTube at a later date. Lectures are free and open to the public. Registration is required.

events.title: After Dark: The Twilight Zone
about: Ready to meet some seriously weird creatures? Venture into the ocean's shadowy depths and discover the research happening in our ocean’s Twilight Zone.

At 6:45 pm, join Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution Scientist Emeritus, Dana Yoerger as he shares Mesobot’s journey into the Twilight Zone At 7:30 pm Harvard Professor Peter Girguis shines the light on the bizarre creatures lurking in the deep—from armored isopods to glowing denizens Explore specimens from the ichthyology collection at Harvard Museum of Comparative Zoology Get hands-on with MIT Sea Grant and discover how democratizing marine technology empowers anyone to explore and sample the waters around us Take inspiration from the twilight zone's trickiest hunters and craft your own bioluminescent creatures using paper circuits and LEDs Wine and specialty beverages from Nashoba Valley Winery and Distillery and small bites from Viet Citron available for purchase

events.title: Author Talk: Carlton Champian - Notes to My Father
about: Join Boston author Carlton Champian for a reading and conversation centered on Notes to My Father, a personal collection exploring fatherhood, absence, grief, and healing.
Participants can expect heartfelt storytelling, space for reflection and discussion, and an opportunity to write a letter of their own. Sharing is optional.

Carlton Champian is a Boston-based author, storyteller, and founder of Champian Studios. His book, Notes to My Father, explores his relationship with his father and his journey toward healing. Through readings and conversation, he invites others to reflect on their own stories.

events.title: Charla En El Grupo De Lectura
about: La mula ciega por Karen Castañeda Una historia inspirada en acontecimientos reales enlaza tres vidas como consecuencia de un plan monstruoso creado por un crimen organizado. Un malhechor, una madre soltera y una mujer arrepentida desarrollan una trama llena de ambición, dolor y justicia. La aventura de María la lleva a destapar un caso terrorífico que conmocionó todos los niveles políticos y sociales en las comunidades fronterizas de El Paso, Texas, y Ciudad Juárez En esta charla vamos a explorar una conversación sobre la frontera, la resiliencia, la injusticia constitucional y la importancia de contar historias que nacen de nuestra comunidad y en nuestra lenguas. Después, tendremos una sesión de preguntas para conversar directamente con la autora.
Copias de La Mula Ciega estarán disponibles en la mesa de circulación. Las copias son limitadas.

We'll look at Brighton up close, answer questions in an interactive Q&A, and offer resources for further research with maps and geography.

events.title: Author Talk: Paul Lewis — Quothing "The Raven"
about: Boston College Professor Emeritus Paul Lewis leads a discussion of his new book, Quothing "The Raven": The First Responses to America's Most Famous Poem.

In 1845, over 5,300 poems were published in American magazines. Most immediately began their deserved descent into oblivion. Poe's "The Raven" stands as the most conspicuous exception to this. But why? What factors influenced the attention devoted to "The Raven" from the day when it was first published? Why was it widely reprinted, praised, criticized, and mocked during the next weeks and months? Why did it inspire parodies that replaced Poe's "saintly bird of yore" with a veritable menagerie of other animals—including an owl, gazelle, turkey, pig, dog, cats, rats, and (eek!) bedbugs? And how did Poe's reputation—as a literary brawler and harsh book reviewer and as a man who struggled with money and alcohol—play into the reception of "The Raven"?
Signed copies of Paul Lewis' Quothing "The Raven": The First Responses to America's Most Famous Poem will be available at this book-launch event.

Paul Lewis is a Professor Emeritus at Boston College, a past president of the Poe Studies Association, and the curator of exhibitions on literary Boston. As the Board of Directors chair of the Edgar Allan Poe Foundation of Boston, Inc., Lewis worked with others to celebrate Poe in the city of his birth by having a square at the intersection of Boylston Street and Charles Street South dedicated to Poe in 2010 and then installing a statue of Poe in it in 2014.

events.title: Author Talk: Steven Levitsky with "How Democracies Die"
about: Join us for this talk with author Steven Levitsky on his book, How Democracies Die. This program is a partnership between the Boston Public Library and the Citywide Friends of the BPL.

The United States’ descent into competitive authoritarianism during the second Trump presidency should never have happened. No democracy even remotely as rich or as old as America’s has ever broken down. American society had more than enough muscle to thwart an authoritarian offensive. But political, business, and civic leaders either acquiesced to the Trump administration’s authoritarian bullying or quietly stepped to the sidelines, allowing Trump’s authoritarian offensive to accelerate. This talk asks why U.S. elites abdicated in the face of an authoritarian threat, explores the prospects for reversing the authoritarian turn, and discusses what we can do to prevent it from happening again.

Steven Levitsky is David Rockefeller Professor of Latin American Studies and Professor of Government and Director of the David Rockefeller Center for Latin American Studies at Harvard. His research focuses on democratization and authoritarianism, political parties, and weak and informal institutions, with a focus on Latin America. He is co-author (with Daniel Ziblatt) of How Democracies Die, which was a New York Times Best-Seller and was published in 30 languages, and Tyranny of the Minority: Why American Democracy Reached the Breaking Point. He has written or edited eleven other books, including Transforming Labor-Based Parties in Latin America: Argentine Peronism in Comparative Perspective (Cambridge University Press 2003), Competitive Authoritarianism: Hybrid Regimes after the Cold War (with Lucan Way) (Cambridge University Press, 2010), and Revolution and Dictatorship: The Violent Origins of Durable Authoritarianism (with Lucan Way) (Princeton University Press, 2022). He is currently writing two books: one on the crisis of American democracy and another on global democratic resilience. Professor Levitsky is a Senior Fellow at the Kettering Foundation. In 2026, he was elected to the American Academy of Arts and Sciences. Professor Levitsky has written for New York Times, The Washington Post, The Atlantic, Foreign Affairs, and The New Republic, and he has been a columnist for La Republica in Peru.

events.title: Author Talk: Jason Allison—The Killing Yards
about: The Fall 2026 Author Talk Series, presented by the Friends of the South End Library, will wrap up with Jason Allison sharing his debut novel, The Killing Yards. Please join us on Wednesday, December 9 starting at 6:30 pm at Union Church (Connection Room, 485 Columbus Ave.) for a fun and lively conversation in this author talk series!
In 1993 New York, reformed drug-trafficker Jimmy Lettner runs Abattoir, Manhattan’s hottest nightspot. All he wants is a clean business, but a city rife with corruption makes that impossible.

Unbeknownst to Jimmy, his right-hand man is running an ecstasy ring inside the club, drawing heat from ruthless rivals and the NYPD. Rookie cop Ben Hopkins goes undercover to make a name for himself, only to get swallowed whole by the gritty scene. As the body count rises and the mayor closes in, Jimmy must embrace his dark past to protect his surviving daughter and save his empire.

Bronx-born and raised, Jason Allison spent twenty years with the NYPD, mostly as a homicide detective. His debut novel,The Killing Yards, will be published by Crooked Lane Books in the fall of 2026. His award-winning fiction has been featured in Fighting Words: Bruisers, Brawlers, and Bad Intentions, Rock and a Hard Place, and New England’s Best Crime Stories.

events.title: Author Talk: Cotten Seiler on “White Care”
about: Join Dickinson College professor Cotten Seiler for a conversation about his new book, White Care. The book discusses how few of us, going about our daily lives, notice the infrastructure that surrounds us and makes those lives possible. What also remains hidden in plain sight is how public infrastructure in the United States has been shaped by theories of race and human evolution. Cotten Seiler’s White Care shows that, from the late 1800s to the present, expert assessments of the quality of the national population have both driven and thwarted the state’s provision of infrastructures of water, sanitation, energy, transportation, recreation, and education. If a nation’s infrastructure is a concrete measure of its belief in its population’s future, what does the current state of American infrastructure say about us?
Lunch will be served and registration is required to attend.

Cotten Seiler is a professor of American Studies at Dickinson College whose work focuses on U.S. cultural and intellectual history, race, feminist and political theory, and infrastructure humanities. He is the author of the books Republic of Drivers: A Cultural History of Automobility in America (Chicago, 2008) and White Care: The Impact of Race on American Infrastructure (Chicago, 2026), coeditor of Engaging Mobilities: Interventions in Pedagogy and Practice (Berghahn, forthcoming 2027), and editor-in-chief of Transfers: Interdisciplinary Journal of Mobility Studies. His essays have appeared in journals such as American Quarterly, Public Culture, Social Text, Reviews in American History, and History & Technology. He is a frequent media commentator on US politics, automobility, race, and infrastructure and can be reached at In discussion with Seiler is Dr. Karilyn Crockett. Crockett's research focuses on large-scale land use changes in twentieth century American cities and examines the social and geographic implications of structural poverty, racial formations and memory. Her book, People before Highways: Boston Activists, Urban Planners, and a New Movement for City Making (UMass Press 2018) investigates a 1960s era grassroots movement to halt urban extension of the U.S. interstate highway system and the geographic and political changes in Boston that resulted. In 2019 this book was named “ten best books about Boston of the decade” by Boston Public Library librarians. Crockett holds a PhD…

events.title: Places Known and Remembered: An Art Exhibition by Laura Gatzos
about: This exhibit by Laura Gatzos, contains depictions of familiar and comforting scenes and places we encounter as New Englanders. From local parks to rural roads, from museums to comforting scenes of home, the paintings in this collection invoke a sense of nostalgia and wonderment and assert that beauty and color are a form of self-care."

Artist Statement: I create art that is detailed, yet calm, brightly colored, yet gentle. In a world that encourages cynicism, sarcasm, and hard edges, my art offers an alternate proposition where kindness is valued, and the restorative properties of the natural world can offer a soothing respite.

I draw and paint the places where I find calm: my family farm and environs in Vermont, where I grew up and return to as often as I can; the Emerald Necklase and conservation lands in the Boston area, where I go when I need an escape; Greece, the homeland of my husband's family, where I am in awe of the beauty of the land, the architecture, and the sea.

Bio: Laura Gatzos has been creating art for as long as she can remember, using pastels, oils, watercolors, and acrylics. Born and raised on a dairy farm in the Northeast Kingdom of Vermont, Laura is inspired by nature and seeks to capture the beauty and restorative properties of the natural world.

Professionally, Laura combines creativity and her love of science, technology, and her previous experience as a medical technologist to support research computing endeavors at the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, finding solutions which promote cost-savings, increase computing efficiency, and improve ease-of-use for members of the DFCI research community.

events.title: The Inevitable Return: Exploding Plastic Revisited
about: On October 29, 1966, the ICA/Boston hosted a groundbreaking multimedia performance by Andy Warhol and the Velvet Underground under the enigmatic title “Exploding Plastic Inevitable.” Presented as part of Warhol’s second-ever museum exhibition, the event invited audiences to experience a cacophony of durational light and sound activations, meant to challenge any expectations of instant pleasure or gratification. The Velvet Underground had become well-known for their dark, minimalist, and occasionally abrasive sound. Among Warhol’s goals for the piece were to explore the capacity to bestow renewed interest upon details that are often submerged in the normative, evenly lit flow of time. In addition to live music, the night consisted of film projections, a variety of strobe and spotlights, and choreographed dance, to create a singular, and confrontational, total-art experience.

On the occasion of “Exploding Plastic Inevitable’s” 60th anniversary and as part of 90 YEARS, the museum’s deep dive into its long and storied history, the ICA resurrects the spirit of what has been called one of the greatest concerts in Boston history. The December 11 event will feature performances and installations by Boston Cream, Caleb Hawkins, The Croaks, Cursed Image, DakouDakou, Organs Studios, Pleasure Coffin, System Failure, and The Dregs Liquid Light Show.

events.title: Dune: Part Three
about: From Warner Bros. Pictures and Legendary Pictures comes Dune: Part Three, bringing Academy Award-nominated filmmaker Denis Villeneuve’s epic trilogy to a breathtaking conclusion.

Dune: Part Three is set nearly two decades after Paul Atreides seized control of the Imperium. Now a ruthless Emperor, Paul must face the consequences of his reign as old allies return, terrifying new threats emerge, and betrayal lurks in every shadow. Haunted by visions of Imperial collapse and the reappearance of his long-lost love, Paul is drawn into a sweeping conspiracy, with Chani at the heart of its unfolding mystery. As rebellion brews and enemies close in, Paul must confront the true cost of power and the fate of those he loves the most.

The film stars Oscar nominee Timothée Chalamet, Zendaya, Jason Momoa, Oscar nominee Florence Pugh, Rebecca Ferguson, Isaach de Bankolé, with Oscar nominee Charlotte Rampling, with Anya Taylor-Joy, and Robert Pattinson, and Oscar winner Javier Bardem.

Villeneuve directs from a screenplay by Villeneuve and Brian K. Vaughan, based on the novels written by Frank Herbert. The film is produced by Oscar nominees Mary Parent, Cale Boyter, Villeneuve and Tanya Lapointe, and Joe Caracciolo, and executive produced by Joshua Grode, Thomas Tull, Herbert W. Gains, Brian Herbert, Byron Merritt, Kim Herbert, Kevin J. Anderson, Richard P. Rubinstein, John Harrison and Jessica Derhammer.

Joining Villeneuve behind the camera are Oscar-winning director of photography Linus Sandgren, Oscar-winning production designer Patrice Vermette, Oscar-winning editor Joe Walker, Oscar nominated costume designer Jacqueline West, Oscar-nominated casting director Francine Maisler, and Oscar-winning composer Hans Zimmer.

Warner Bros. Pictures and Legendary Pictures Present A Legendary Pictures Production, A Film By Denis Villeneuve, Dune: Part Three, only in cinemas December 17, 2026. The film will be distributed worldwide by Warner Bros. Pictures and in China by Legendary East.
Directed by Denis Villeneuve · 2h 25m

events.title: White Christmas
about: Join West Newton Cinema for a musical matinee! Our monthly pick will vary from beloved classics to jazz, from vaudeville to psychedelic rock, brought to you by the imaginative skill of artists able to make scenes look the way great music feels. We’ll feature films from the Golden Age of Hollywood musicals, with surprises that transcend the era and define others. The cinematic brilliance of these films has never left us. In fact, seeing them again, or for the first time, will reinvigorate your love for the movie musical and send you out of the theater tapping your feet.

With its timeless Irving Berlin musical numbers—including its iconic title track—White Christmas is a holiday classic for a reason. In scenes shimmering with superstar performances, we watch as Bing Crosby and Danny Kaye join forces, dancingly and romantically, with sister-act Rosemary Clooney and Vera-Ellen to save a struggling Vermont ski-resort owned by Dean Jagger’s retired Major General. Directed by Hollywood vet Michael Curtiz (Casablanca, The Adventures of Robin Hood), White Christmas is chock-full of memorable moments and infectious tunes, wrapping the holiday season into one perfect Hollywood package that’s sure to put anyone in the Christmas spirit.
2h 0m

From boundary-pushing directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim comes You Can See Everything.
Directed by Lance Oppenheim, Nathan Fielder · 2h 54m

events.title: Local Spotlight: Cut To David
about: Join us for a one-day only community screening of Cut to David followed by a post-film discussion with the filmmaker Sandy Jaffe and family, and other participants in the film.

David’s story is beautifully layered from the start: An adopted, Chinese-American, transgender teen, raised in a Jewish home in Boston with a filmmaker for a mom, with a camera always close by. As David journeys from high school to college to adulthood, Sandy Jaffe’s camera documents her family’s evolving relationship as each participant has a turn steering the narrative. Blending vérité footage, home videos, and candid conversations, the film begins as an effort to understand David’s gender transition and expands into a deeper exploration of identity, agency, authorship, power, and the complicated yet loving bond between a mother and her son. An intimate, fly-on-the-wall documentary, CUT TO DAVID considers the possibilities—and perils—of living visibly and openly, exploring how ethnicity, gender, religion, and parenting shape who we become.

Sandy Jaffe is a filmmaker and writer, and has taught screenwriting at various institutions in the Boston area. Her first documentary feature, Our Mockingbird, was a part of the PBS series America Reframed. She is a co-facilitator of a parent support group through Greater Boston PFLAG. Cut to David, her second feature documentary, premiered to a sold out audience at GlobeDocs 2026.

Jay Blitzman is a former public defender who specialized in representing youth and late teens. He served for 24 years as a juvenile court judge, retiring as the First Justice of the Middlesex Division of the MA Juvenile Court. He teaches law, consults on youth and criminal issues, and advocates for supporting youth voice and agency in all contexts.

David Blitzman graduated Magna Cum Laude from Ithaca College in 2020. He received his MSW in 2025 from Smith College School of Social Work, and works as a therapist in Greater Boston. David also volunteers for organizations which promote community engagement and collaboration.
1h 10m

events.title: Wild Horse Nine
about: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris (John Malkovich) and Lee (Sam Rockwell) are dispatched from Santiago to Easter island by their bureau chief, MJ (Steve Buscemi). Amongst the Island's iconic statues, and as the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies, Chris's newfound bond with a pair of rebellious students (Mariana di Girolamo and Ailín Salas) threatens to send everyone’s trip to this remote paradise sideways.
Directed by Martin McDonagh · 1h 58m

events.title: Minotaur
about: Intrigue, corruption, betrayal, survival: the walls of the maze are closing in.
The latest from Academy Award® nominated writer-director Andrey Zvyagintsev (Loveless, Leviathan), Cannes Grand Prix winner MINOTAUR is a twist-laden parable for our times.

Russia, 2022. Amidst the comfortable trappings of affluence and domesticity, corporate executive Gleb (Dmitriy Mazurov) finds himself under siege on all fronts. At home, he is haunted by suspicions that his increasingly distant wife Galina (Iris Lebedeva) is unfaithful. At work, he contends with a demand from local authorities to draft a quota of employees for the war in Ukraine. Desperate to keep his hands clean, Gleb struggles to reassert control even as the collapse of his carefully ordered life seems fated to accelerate toward violence.

A pressure cooker in cinematic form, MINOTAUR uncovers and indicts the heart of societal darkness with searing clarity. Uniting intimately-drawn performances and stark visual power, this is peerless work from an indisputable master.
Directed by Andrey Zviaguintsev, Andrey Zvyagintsev · 2h 15m

events.title: Fatherland
about: FATHERLAND centres on the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann (Hanns Zischler) and his daughter Erika (Sandra Hüller) - actress, writer and rally driver. In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, father and daughter embark on a challenging and emotional road trip in a black Buick taking them across a Germany in ruins - from US dominated Frankfurt to Soviet controlled Weimar. Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the US, Thomas Mann has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also a deep fracture within his own family.

With FATHERLAND, director Paweł Pawlikowski picks up where he left off with his award-winning IDA and COLD WAR, exploring – in his elliptic, distilled style - the themes of identity, family, love and guilt amid the turmoil and confusion of post-war Europe.
Directed by Paweł Pawlikowski · 1h 22m

events.title: I Play Rocky
about: I PLAY ROCKY is an electrifying true story about an unknown actor with an unshakable belief that he wasn't just meant to write Rocky--he was meant to be Rocky Balboa. Told "no" at every turn, Sylvester Stallone bets everything on himself, holding the line on playing the lead against seemingly impossible odds. The result is the ultimate underdog story behind the ultimate underdog movie.
Directed by Peter Farrelly · 2h 8m

events.title: Yury Butusov's "King Lear"
about: Presented in Russian with English subtitles RUNTIME: 3 hours 34 minutes (Includes a 10 minute intermission)

Yury Butusov’s visionary production shifts focus away from political tyranny to examine the agonizing collapse of generational bonds. On Maxim Obrezkov's barren stage hangs a massive, swaying moon as the world tilts off its axis. Artur Ivanov portrays a physically imposing Lear trapped between life and death from the start, unraveling alongside Victor Dobronravov’s Gloucester and Sergei Volkov’s cynical Edmund. Evgenia Kregzhde doubles magnificently as both Cordelia and the Fool. Driven by a sweeping, thunderous soundtrack, this interpretation turns the tragedy into a visceral, intense nightmare about human loneliness.

Yury Butusov (1961–2025) was one of the most influential and innovative theatre directors of his generation. Renowned for his emotionally charged visual language, bold reinterpretations of classical texts, and fearless experimentation, Butusov profoundly influenced contemporary European theatre. After leaving Russia in 2022, he continued to create productions across Europe until his death in August of 2025.

events.title: Hexed
about: In Walt Disney Animation Studios' all-new magical coming-of-age saga, “Hexed,” an impulsive and unconventional teenage girl named Billie (voice of Hailee Steinfeld) discovers secret magical abilities which, once unleashed, hurtle her into a spectacle-filled journey out of suburbia and into a vast witch realm called Hexe. Forced to team up with her cautious mother, Alice (voice of Rashida Jones), they uncover family mysteries that could change the world of witches forever. Directed by Fawn Veerasunthorn and Jason Hand, co-directed by Josie Trinidad and produced by Roy Conli, Disney’s “Hexed” opens exclusively in theaters November 25, 2026.
Directed by Fawn Veerasunthorn, Jason Hand, Josie Trinidad · 1h 49m

about: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris and Lee are dispatched from Santiago to Easter Island by their bureau chief, MJ. Amongst the Island's iconic statues, and as the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies, Chris's newfound bond with a pair of rebellious students threatens to send everyone’s trip to this remote paradise sideways.

events.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
about: Harry Lehman is an aging pickpocket who plies his trade with ever-diminishing returns in a drastically changed New York. Wallets stuffed with cash have been replaced by easily cancelled credit cards, and Harry struggles to make ends meet as he cares for his disabled wife, Rosie. When he unwittingly purloins and fences a valuable USB stick, Harry finds himself in a race against time to return the loot or face the rage of a vengeful crime family.

events.title: Hexed

Forced to team up with her cautious mother, Alice, they uncover family mysteries that could change the world of witches forever.

about: Barbara Stanwyck stars as a famous expert on marriage, cooking and homemaking who is asked by her publisher to host a national hero for Christmas dinner at her famous Connecticut home. events.title: Touch of Evil
about: A car-bomb murder blows the lid off police corruption in a pestilent border town, resulting in a three-ring circus of a film noir that fizzled on release, but is now seen, on its own seamy merits, to rival Citizen Kane in filmmaking audacity. Using actor/writer/director Orson Welles's 58-page memo of suggested changes as a blueprint, Touch of Evil has been reconstructed to the 110-minute version originally envisioned by the late director. Charlton Heston, Janet Leigh and Marlene Dietrich also star.
1h 51m

events.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping
about: From acclaimed director Francis Lawrence, THE HUNGER GAMES: SUNRISE ON THE REAPING follows sixteen-year-old Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) from District 12, beginning on the morning of the reaping for the 50th Annual Hunger Games, also known as the Second Quarter Quell, the biggest Games yet with twice as many tributes.

Set in the world of Panem 24 years before the events of The Hunger Games, the story follows Haymitch into the arena, where he forms an unlikely alliance with fellow tribute Maysilee Donner (Mckenna Grace) and joins a coalition determined to challenge the Capitol’s control under President Snow (Ralph Fiennes). As the competition unfolds, Haymitch risks everything to take down the Games from within the arena — setting in motion the rebellion that will change Panem forever.
2h 38m

about: From acclaimed director Francis Lawrence, THE HUNGER GAMES: SUNRISE ON THE REAPING follows sixteen-year-old Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) from District 12, beginning on the morning of the reaping for the 50th Annual Hunger Games, also known as the Second Quarter Quell, the biggest Games yet with twice as many tributes.

Set in the world of Panem 24 years before the events of The Hunger Games, the story follows Haymitch into the arena, where he forms an unlikely alliance with fellow tribute Maysilee Donner (Mckenna Grace) and joins a coalition determined to challenge the Capitol’s control under President Snow (Ralph Fiennes). As the competition unfolds, Haymitch risks everything to take down the Games from within the arena — setting in motion the rebellion that will change Panem forever.

events.title: The Metropolitan Opera: Samson et Dalila (2026)
about: Sacred, scandalous, and irresistibly alluring, Saint-Saëns’s spectacular take on the biblical hero of legendary strength and the seductive Philistine whose beauty overpowers him returns in the Met’s larger-than-life production. Featuring a massive orchestra and chorus and some of opera’s most spellbinding tunes, this masterpiece of French grand opera is a feast for the eyes and ears, with an electrifying cast led by the formidable star pairing of mezzo-soprano Aigul Akhmetshina and tenor Clay Hilley, who makes a notable company debut.
3h 54m

events.title: The Metropolitan Opera: The Magic Flute Holiday Encore (2026)
about: The Met made history in December 2006 when it presented its first Live in HD transmission to cinemas worldwide: the abridged English-language version of Mozart’s The Magic Flute. Julie Taymor’s whimsical production features a winning ensemble—including tenor Matthew Polenzani, baritone Nathan Gunn, and bass René Pape—and returns to select movie theaters for a special encore presentation during the holiday season.
1h 56m

events.title: The Royal Ballet - The Nutcracker (2025)
about: At a cosy Christmas party, young Clara meets the mysterious magician Drosselmeyer, who gives her a nutcracker doll. When the guests have departed and the house is asleep, Clara sneaks downstairs in search of the doll. Instead, she finds Drosselmeyer, who whisks her away on a journey into a whole world of enchantment: fantastical landscapes of flurried snow and glittering confection where toys come alive and the magic never stops.

Recorded live at the Royal Opera House in 2025, Peter Wright’s production of this festive family favourite sparkles to the wondrous swell of Tchaikovsky’s orchestral score, alongside the glow and grandeur of Julia Trevelyan Oman’s period designs.
2h 10m

events.title: Kimberly Bartosik: bLUr
about: bLUr, choreographed by Kimberly Bartosik, is a highly physical and emotionally intense dance piece in which five performers navigate scenes of desire, care, violence, and tender rescue.

Exploring the haunting impact of witnessing a loved one’s overdose, but moving beyond explicit narratives of the opioid crisis, the work uses visceral movement cycles to embody the violent cravings and internal battles of substance abuse. Built out of Bartosik’s own experiences and deeply shaped by the individuality of her performers, bLUr is both personal and universal as it warps time and reminds us of our fragility, power, and need for one another.

Kimberly Bartosik is a choreographer, performer, educator, and writer. As a member of the Merce Cunningham Dance Company for nine years, Bartosik received a Bessie Award for Exceptional Artistry. She is currently an Advisor for The Ailey School/Fordham BFA Program and teaches at SUNY/Purchase and the Merce Cunningham Trust.

She is a 2024 National Dance Project Production Grant (NDP) recipient from the New England Foundation for the Arts; a 2025 New York State Council on the Arts/NYSCA Support for Artists Award grantee with support of the Office of the Governor and the New York State Legislature; and a 2025 Harkness Foundation for Dance Project Grant recipient, among numerous other awards. Bartosik’s work has been commissioned and presented by BAM Next Wave, New York Live Arts, Crossing the Line Festival, Bates Dance Festival, Torn Space Theater, American Dance Festival, LUMBERYARD, American Realness, Abrons Art Center, Gibney, Danspace Project, The Kitchen, La Mama, and others. She has toured to Supersense: Festival of the Ecstatic (Melbourne, Australia), Bratislava in Movement (Slovakia), Wexner Arts Center, Dance Place, American Dance Festival, The Yard, MASS MoCA/Jacob’s Pillow, Flynn Space, Bates Dance Festival, Columbia College, Centre Chorégraphique National de Franche-Comté à Belfort, Festival Rencontres chorégraphique internationales de Seine-Saint Denis, Artdanthe Festival, Church, Mount Tremper Arts, and others.
This program is supported in part by the Irene Hunter Fund for Dance at MASS MoCA in association with Jacob’s Pillow.
bLUr was co-commissioned by L’Alliance New York’s Crossing the Line Festival and by ADF/American Dance Festival with support from the Doris Duke/SHS Foundations Award for New Works. bLUr is also…

events.title: Weave, Repair, Connect
about: Dip your toes into the world of textiles during MASS MoCA’s Textile Repair Salon! Join regional practitioners Jena Duncan and Elsa Cousins from Swanson’s Fabrics Stash House and MASS MoCA museum educators for a casual evening of textile repair, embroidery, and small-scale weaving.

Participants are welcome to bring textile objects or clothing in need of repair and learn the skills to mend them with support from the Swanson’s Fabric teaching staff. Mending is for everyone; no sewing experience is required! This project aspires to build an exciting culture of clothing reuse and repair by empowering and inspiring our local community to learn how to make, mend, and maintain their clothing and textiles. This workshop is also for community members concerned about the sustainability and environmental impact of textiles who may not see themselves as able to sew.

If you don’t have a repair, don’t worry! MASS MoCA Museum Educators will give instruction on small-scale weaving and invite participants to contribute to our community weaving project currently on view.

Bring your friends, bring a date. Refreshments are available to purchase from MASS MoCA’s bar. No experience required; all materials included, although participants are welcome to bring their own and share with others.

Jena Duncan (they/them) is a fiber arts artist passionate about community building. They share sewing as a liberatory and healing practice to feel more at home in our bodies and help keep textiles out of the landfill by extending their use. Jena founded Blushing Mustard Studios in Greenfield’s Madhouse Multi-Arts, offering gender- and fat- affirming clothing alterations, repairs, and custom commissions. They teach sewing and mending classes at Swanson’s Fabrics, a second-hand textile store and education center in Turners Falls. Jena also works as an art installer and fabricator, helping artists bring their work to life, most recently at MASS MoCA, MCLA’s Gallery 51, and UMASS’s University Museum of Contemporary Art.

Elsa Cousins, Director of Education at Swanson’s Fabrics, is an artist and educator teaching mending and sewing classes at Swanson’s Fabrics Stash House, local libraries, and community spaces, as well as environmental science classes at UMass Amherst and Holyoke Community College. events.title: Machine Dazzle: Changes
events.detail: The Costume Design for Taylor Mac’s A 24-Decade History of Popular Music
about: Machine Dazzle has been creating extraordinary costumes for over 30 years. As an artist, costume designer, set designer, and performance artist, he has presented his genre-defying work at venues ranging from Broadway to the runway, wowing audiences from Joe’s Pub to the Museum of Arts and Design in New York. As the nation marks 250 years of America’s history, MASS MoCA will showcase wearable sculptural looks by the artist that examine the 24 decades since the founding of the United States in 1776.

Machine Dazzle created this collection for Taylor Mac’s Pulitzer Prize-nominated A 24-Decade History of Popular Music — a singular 24-hour performance art concert that looks at the nation’s stories through a queer lens, giving voice to the marginalized communities often left out of mainstream historical narratives. The costumes incorporate images and objects that reference political movements, social histories, and inventions from each time period. Many of the materials in the garments are cast- offs that the artist transforms into elaborate and stunning visions that simultaneously speak to material culture. The artist describes his approach as applying “glitter to litter.”

For his designs, Machine Dazzle was a co-recipient of the 2017 Bessie Award for Outstanding Visual Design, a Henry Hewes Design Award by The American Theatre Wing, and the TDF/Irene Sharaff Ascending Artist Award (formerly known as the Kitty Leech Ascending Artist Award)in recognition of his success in the field of costume design. The original 24-hour stage production has been adapted into an HBO Original Documentary Film directed by Jeffrey Friedman and Rob Epstein and co-produced by Pomegranate Arts for which Machine Dazzle won a 2024 Emmy Award for Outstanding Costume Design.
This exhibition is a collaboration between MASS MoCA, Pomegranate Arts, and Wrightwood 659.

Image:Portrait of Taylor Mac (detail) in A 24-Decade History of Popular Music: 1816-1826: Decade 5: Songs Popular in Recovery, 2022, Costume Design by Machine Dazzle. Photo by Gregory Kramer. Courtesy of Pomegranate Arts.

events.title: Club Kid
about: A hard-partying New York City club promoter (writer/director Jordan Firstman) sees his whirlwind lifestyle upended by the arrival of the 10-year-old son he never knew he had.

“CLUB KID turns out to be a deeply sincere movie about the feeling of having stayed too long at the fair and what it takes to move forward, and how growing up can be both great and gutting. Everybody loves a good party. But life when the lights come up can be beautiful, too.” Alissa Wilkinson. A New York Times Critic's Pick!
Directed by Jordan Firstman · R

events.title: Fatherland
about: At the height of the Cold War, the writer Thomas Mann and his daughter—actress, writer, and rally driver—Erika embark on a road trip in a black Buick cruiser across a divided Germany in ruins, traveling from the Allied-occupied city of Frankfurt to Soviet-controlled Weimar.
The new film from director Paweł Pawlikowski (IDA, COLD WAR) stars Sandra Hüller (ANATOMY OF A FALL) and Hanns Zischler (MUNICH).
“A film of deep, luminous feeling... Huller’s ability to let you into her characters’ thinking is a marvel.” Manohla Dargis. A New York Times Critic's Pick!
Directed by Paweł Pawlikowski · NR

events.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
about: A decade after his death, genre-defying filmmaker William Greaves has one last trick up his sleeve with what he considered the most important event he captured on film: a 1972 party he engineered with the living luminaries of the Harlem Renaissance.

For four hours, this extraordinary group—many of whom had not seen each other in fifty years—reminisced, critiqued, argued, laughed and drank while wrestling with their place in a rapidly shifting cultural landscape.

Shot on 16mm film, newly restored and now directed by Greaves’ son David, this landmark film is at once a self-exploration and an inquiry into the heart of the critical mass of energy called the Harlem Renaissance.

William GreaDisable rich-textves’ intent was not only to document these artists and intellectuals as they spoke about their lives and work but also to plumb the meaning of the extraordinary creative period in which they lived to help us better understand how culture has been passed on from one generation to another and the role that the artist plays in keeping it alive.

“The movie flows beautifully, with a seamless mix of found and originally shot material... The past comes vibrantly alive in these rooms, but always circles back to the present and often points to the future.” Manohla Dargis. A New York Times Critic's Pick!
Directed by David Greaves, Liani Greaves, William Greaves · PG-13

events.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
about: Harry Lehman (John Turturro) is an aging pickpocket who plies his trade with ever-diminishing returns in a drastically changed New York.
Wallets stuffed with cash have been replaced by easily canceled credit cards, and Harry struggles to make ends meet as he cares for his disabled wife, Rosie.
When he unwittingly purloins and fences a valuable USB stick, Harry finds himself in a race against time to return the loot or face the rage of a vengeful crime family.

“THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is remarkable in many ways, first among them Turturro’s performance. Somehow, despite a 40-year career full of memorable roles, Turturro is still underrated. This movie lets him showcase all of his best qualities; he gets to be quick-witted and fleet-footed, but also full of love and grief.” Alissa Wilkinson. A New York Times Critic's Pick!
Directed by Noah Segan · R

events.title: Wild Horse Nine
about: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris (John Malkovich) and Lee (Sam Rockwell) are dispatched from Santiago to Easter island by their bureau chief, MJ (Steve Buscemi).

Amongst the Island's iconic statues, and as the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies, Chris's newfound bond with a pair of rebellious students (Mariana di Girolamo and Ailín Salas) threatens to send everyone’s trip to this remote paradise sideways.
WILD HORSE NINE is the new film from writer/director Martin McDonagh (THE BANSHEES OF INISHERIN, IN BRUGES).

“Elegiac and delightfully foul-mouthed, the film is both a political thriller and a meditation on the nature of legacy, memory and what makes life worth living, anchored by a career-best performance from Malkovich, who is never better than when he’s playing a villainous but lovable rascal”
“A bittersweet hangout film about lonely, crumpled men facing up to mortality, dealing with the consequences of violence and chewing the fat to outlandishly funny effect.”
Directed by Martin McDonagh · R

Shot on 16mm film, newly restored and now directed by Greaves’ son David, this landmark film is at once a self-exploration and an inquiry into the heart of the critical mass of energy called the Harlem Renaissance.

William GreaDisable rich-textves’ intent was not only to document these artists and intellectuals as they spoke about their lives and work but also to plumb the meaning of the extraordinary creative period in which they lived to help us better understand how culture has been passed on from one generation to another and the role that the artist plays in keeping it alive.

“The movie flows beautifully, with a seamless mix of found and originally shot material... The past comes vibrantly alive in these rooms, but always circles back to the present and often points to the future.” Manohla Dargis. A New York Times Critic's Pick!
Directed by David Greaves, Liani Greaves, William Greaves · PG-13

events.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
about: Harry Lehman (John Turturro) is an aging pickpocket who plies his trade with ever-diminishing returns in a drastically changed New York.
Wallets stuffed with cash have been replaced by easily canceled credit cards, and Harry struggles to make ends meet as he cares for his disabled wife, Rosie.
When he unwittingly purloins and fences a valuable USB stick, Harry finds himself in a race against time to return the loot or face the rage of a vengeful crime family.

“THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is remarkable in many ways, first among them Turturro’s performance. Somehow, despite a 40-year career full of memorable roles, Turturro is still underrated. This movie lets him showcase all of his best qualities; he gets to be quick-witted and fleet-footed, but also full of love and grief.” Alissa Wilkinson. A New York Times Critic's Pick!
Directed by Noah Segan · R

events.title: Wild Horse Nine
about: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris (John Malkovich) and Lee (Sam Rockwell) are dispatched from Santiago to Easter island by their bureau chief, MJ (Steve Buscemi).

Amongst the Island's iconic statues, and as the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies, Chris's newfound bond with a pair of rebellious students (Mariana di Girolamo and Ailín Salas) threatens to send everyone’s trip to this remote paradise sideways.
WILD HORSE NINE is the new film from writer/director Martin McDonagh (THE BANSHEES OF INISHERIN, IN BRUGES).

“Elegiac and delightfully foul-mouthed, the film is both a political thriller and a meditation on the nature of legacy, memory and what makes life worth living, anchored by a career-best performance from Malkovich, who is never better than when he’s playing a villainous but lovable rascal”
“A bittersweet hangout film about lonely, crumpled men facing up to mortality, dealing with the consequences of violence and chewing the fat to outlandishly funny effect.”
Directed by Martin McDonagh · R

events.title: Club Kid
about: A hard-partying New York City club promoter (writer/director Jordan Firstman) sees his whirlwind lifestyle upended by the arrival of the 10-year-old son he never knew he had.

“CLUB KID turns out to be a deeply sincere movie about the feeling of having stayed too long at the fair and what it takes to move forward, and how growing up can be both great and gutting. Everybody loves a good party. But life when the lights come up can be beautiful, too.” Alissa Wilkinson. A New York Times Critic's Pick!
Directed by Jordan Firstman · R

events.title: Fatherland
about: At the height of the Cold War, the writer Thomas Mann and his daughter—actress, writer, and rally driver—Erika embark on a road trip in a black Buick cruiser across a divided Germany in ruins, traveling from the Allied-occupied city of Frankfurt to Soviet-controlled Weimar.
The new film from director Paweł Pawlikowski (IDA, COLD WAR) stars Sandra Hüller (ANATOMY OF A FALL) and Hanns Zischler (MUNICH).
“A film of deep, luminous feeling... Huller’s ability to let you into her characters’ thinking is a marvel.” Manohla Dargis. A New York Times Critic's Pick!
Directed by Paweł Pawlikowski · NR

events.title: The Exquisite Hour, Part 2
about: This screening is free to the general public. Tickets are available only at the Amherst Cinema box office on a first-come, first-served basis. They can be picked up in advance during the Cinema’s regular box office hours, or at the door the evening of the screening.
Following an inaugural program in February 2026, this screening features a set of 16mm experimental films that harness the beauties and intensities of photochemical filmmaking.

“The Exquisite Hour” takes its name from a film originally completed by Phil Solomon in 1989, which was intended, in part, as a rumination on the impending death of celluloid film. Nearly forty years later, the filmic medium is still alive due in no small measure to an experimental film tradition that has been expanding the aesthetic capacities of photochemical filmmaking for decades.

The second edition of “The Exquisite Hour” showcases six contributions to this tradition that were created by artists from different generations and locales. While these works employ varied formats, techniques, and methodologies, they all share an investment in the future of analog film culture, which this program seeks to affirm and extend.
Films will be projected from a mix of 16mm and digital.
Curated by Abraham Ravett, Professor of Film and Photography, Hampshire College, and Josh Guilford, Assistant Professor of English in Film and Media Studies, Amherst College.
Presented in partnership with the English Department and Film and Media Studies Program at Amherst College.

Magdalena Bermudez, 2025, 16mm on digital, b&w, sound, 12 min “Women pretend to be rocks. Military operations masquerade as art education. One woman deserts to pursue a more radical act of unselfing.” –Magdalena Bermudez Ericka Beckman, 2002, 16mm, color, sound, 10 min “Switch Center is a tribute to the futuristic architecture of the Soviet post war period, and a reaction to seeing it transitioned to shopping malls or global corporate office structures. I was invited by Balazs Bela Studio in Budapest to produce a short experimental film in Hungary. I was the first American artist to be invited by this famous film collective after the fall of Soviet power. The collaboration took place in August 2000, culminating in Switch Center, a ten minute experimental documentary shot in many defunct Danube Water Works locations on the outskirts of Budapest. The architecture of a 1960's water…
Directed by various

events.title: Elsinore
about: Andrew Scott delivers his strongest performance honoring the real-life story of Ian Charleson, the CHARIOTS OF FIRE actor who courageously pushed through AIDS to play Hamlet at London’s National Theatre.
Facing his own mortality with unflinching honesty, wit, and grace, Charleson delivers a courageous performance that becomes a source of healing and inspiration for those around him.

“Scott is one of the most mesmerizing actors working today, and even by his standards he’s splendid in this role. The story sounds depressing, potentially even maudlin, but he brings a vibrancy and humor to Charleson that makes his moments of pain and pathos even more affecting.” Alissa Wilkinson. A New York Times Critic's Pick!
Directed by Simon Stone · R

events.title: The Beastmaster
about: Calling all dungeon masters! The follow-up to PHANTASM from young filmmaker Don Coscarelli, THE BEASTMASTER is a sublime thrill-ride in the 1980s sword-and-sorcery sweepstakes. It's also the only one that was photographed by John Alcott, the Oscar-winning, Kubrick favorite DP who filmed THE SHINING and A CLOCKWORK ORANGE.

Dar (Marc Singer) is the crown prince of a family that was slaughtered by a lords of evil. When he grows to manhood, Dar cultivates the ability to communicate with animals and seeks revenge on the monstrous priest known as Maax (Rip Torn).
Like CONAN THE BARBARIAN and KRULL, THE BEASTMASTER is an over-the-top mix of fantasy, action, and horror that could only have been birthed in the 1980s.
Directed by Don Coscarelli · PG

events.title: NT Live: Golden Boy
about: Josh O’Connor (The Crown; CHALLENGERS) leads the cast in this searing revival of Clifford Odets’ knockout American classic.

1930s New York, at the height of the Depression. Joe Bonaparte is a gifted young violinist with a future in music, until a chance at fame and fortune lures him into the brutal world of professional boxing. He must confront what he’s willing to sacrifice, who he’s willing to become and how to find his place in a world that demands he choose a side.

Brought to life with a live string quartet and filmed live from the Almeida Theatre. Olivier Award-winner Sam Yates (NT Live: Vanya) directs this propulsive drama exploring ambition, identity, and the high price of success.
Runtime includes a 15-minute intermission.
Directed by Sam Yates · NR

events.title: Emerging Filmmakers of Western Massachusetts 2026
about: This screening is free to the general public. Tickets are available only at the Amherst Cinema box office on a first-come, first-served basis. They can be picked up in advance during the Cinema’s regular box office hours, or at the door the evening of the screening.

The Easthampton Film Festival co-presents a lively selection of narrative and documentary shorts made by Western Massachusetts-based filmmakers, offering audiences an opportunity to experience stories rooted in places, people, and issues they know firsthand.

A panel of featured filmmakers joins us for a post-screening conversation led by Kt Baldassaro, Head of the Easthampton Film Festival Horror Film Subcommittee, Festival Moderator, and Public Ambassador.
Presented in partnership with the Easthampton Film Festival.
A man drives to Chicago to meet Frank, who doesn't answer his calls.
dir. Dinah Mack and Kate Way This documentary short tells the story of the restoration of the historic Holyoke Clock Tower.
Through a series of interactions within a liminal space, a man struggles to break free from the attention-grabbing devices of his companion.
dir. Lucas Fappiano and Colin Hodgson A short documentary about the re-opening of a beloved local live music venue and the lasting impact it continues to have on the community.

dir. Jordan Brooks and Brian Jones A lost man in a crumbling marriage discovers through a chance encounter that traveling back in time may actually be possible, he's faced with a choice: to change the past risking an uncertain future, or reclaim the path he's already on.
The youngest member of a combined family of nine navigates moving houses for the very first time. Presented in five chapters, documented by her older brothers over the course of a year.
This program is supported in part by a grant from the Amherst Cultural Council, a local agency which is supported by the Mass Cultural Council, a state agency.
Directed by various · NR

events.title: Joybubbles
about: Director Rachael J. Morrison, a Hampshire College alum, joins us for a post-film discussion.
This screening is free to Amherst Cinema Members.
JOYBUBBLES is a documentary about a boy who discovers he can control the global telephone system by whistling a magic tone.
Born blind and yearning for connection, his early obsession with the telephone sparks a subculture that shapes the future of hacking and technology.
An official selection of the 2026 Sundance Film Festival.
Please note that this film is presented with open audio description and open captions.
Bellwether is presented with support from Hotel UMass.
Directed by Rachael J. Morrison · NR

events.title: Tokyo Godfathers
about: In modern-day Tokyo, three homeless people’s lives are changed forever when they discover a baby girl at a garbage dump on Christmas Eve. As the New Year fast approaches, these three forgotten members of society band together to solve the mystery of the abandoned child and the fate of her parents. Along the way, encounters with seemingly unrelated events and people force them to confront their own haunted pasts, as they learn to face their future, together.
Join us for a holiday-adjacent animé from the director of PERFECT BLUE and PAPRIKA, co-written by Keiko Nobumoto (COWBOY BEBOP) and featuring a whimsical score by Keiichi Suzuki.
TOKYO GODFATHERS is a masterpiece by turns heartfelt, hilarious and highly original, a tale of hope and redemption in the face of seemingly insurmountable odds.
Directed by Satoshi Kon · PG-13

events.title: The Muppet Christmas Carol
about: Please note that passes cannot be redeemed for this screening.
The Muppets put their spin on the tale of Ebenezer Scrooge (Michael Caine), a Christmas-hating miser visited by three spirits.
They foretell his future and share secrets from his past and present, helping to change his view on life.
Brian Henson, the son of Muppet founder Jim Henson, took over directing duties after the untimely death of his father for THE MUPPET CHRISTMAS CAROL, a unique re-telling of the Charles Dickens tale.

The $5 Family Films series is supported in part by Greenfield Savings Bank and a grant from the Amherst Cultural Council, a local agency which is supported by the Mass Cultural Council, a state agency.

Different films will be appropriate for different children at different ages. We recommend Common Sense Media or the Parents Guide section of as helpful resources in determining what's right for your child.
Directed by Brian Henson · G

events.title: The Apartment
events.detail: Billy Wilder presented by Nina Kleinberg
about: Join us this fall for three films by Billy Wilder, featuring introductions by local film expert Nina Kleinberg.
For this final screening, Nina examines the visual style of the film and discusses how THE APARTMENT challenged the Hays Code.

In 1960, following the success of their collaboration on SOME LIKE IT HOT, director Billy Wilder reteamed with actor Jack Lemmon for what many consider the pinnacle of their respective careers: THE APARTMENT.

C.C. Bud Baxter (Lemmon) is a lowly Manhattan office drone with a lucrative sideline in renting out his apartment to adulterous company bosses and their mistresses. When Bud enters into a similar arrangement with the firm's personnel director, J.D. Sheldrake (Fred MacMurray), his career prospects begin to look up... and up. But when he discovers that Sheldrake's mistress is Fran Kubelik (Shirley MacLaine), the girl of his dreams, he finds himself forced to choose between his career and the woman he loves...
Winner of five Oscars, including Best Picture, THE APARTMENT features a wealth of Hollywood's finest talent on both sides of the camera at the top of their game.

About Nina Kleinberg: In the late 1960s, Nina attended film school at the University of Southern California. She then spent most of the 1970s working in the film industry in Los Angeles, mostly as an editor. Although she went on to a different career, she never gave up her love of film history and the film-making process.

Many of you know Nina from her appearances at Amherst Cinema, including her 2015 film series Film School in 90 Minutes, her 2016 series Out of this World on 1950s science fiction films, her 2019 series Print the Legend on classic Westerns, or her Science on Screen presentation on SINGIN' IN THE RAIN. Her seminar on CASABLANCA is a perpetual favorite with Amherst Cinema audiences, with many repeat viewers. In the fall of 2025, Nina introduced a popular series of three Pre-Code Classics.
Directed by Billy Wilder · NR

events.title: Carol
about: Therese Belivet (Rooney Mara), a young woman in her 20s, is a clerk working in a Manhattan department store and dreaming of a more fulfilling life when she meets Carol (Cate Blanchett), an alluring woman trapped in a loveless, convenient marriage.

After an immediate connection sparks between them, the innocence of their first encounter dims and their connection deepens. As conventional norms of the time challenge their undeniable attraction, an honest story emerges to reveal the resilience of the heart in the face of change.

In an adaptation of Patricia Highsmith’s seminal novel The Price of Salt, CAROL follows two women from very different backgrounds who find themselves in an unexpected love affair in 1950s New York. With much of the story set during the holiday season, this drama has become a Christmas-adjacent classic for grown-ups.

CAROL is directed by Todd Haynes (FAR FROM HEAVEN, I'M NOT THERE) and written by Phyllis Nagy, with moving performances from Blanchett, Mara, Sarah Paulson, Kyle Chandler, Jake Lacy, and Cory Michael Smith.

"At once ardent and analytical, cerebral and swooning, CAROL is a study in human magnetism, in the physics and optics of eros. With sparse dialogue and restrained drama, the film is a symphony of angles and glances, of colors and shadows." A.O. Scott. A New York Times Critics' Pick!
Directed by Todd Haynes · R

events.title: Gremlins
about: With its Christmas lights and dusting of snow, Kingston Falls is an idyllic small town—until the gremlins take over.

A father returns from Chinatown with an unusual pet called a Mogawai as a gift for his son. The rules are simple: Keep your Mogwai away from water, bright lights and, most importantly, never feed him after midnight.
But the rules are inadvertently broken, and the consequences multiply at an alarming rate.
Directed by Joe Dante · PG

events.title: It's A Wonderful Life
about: This 1946 release marked director Frank Capra's return to features after four years of turning out propaganda films for the government, and Capra poured his heart and soul into it.

James Stewart stars as a small-town nobody, on the brink of suicide, who believes his life is worthless. Guardian angel Henry Travers shows him how wrong he is by letting Stewart see what would have happened had he never been born.

Wonderfully drawn and acted by a superb cast (Donna Reed, Beulah Bondi, Thomas Mitchell, Lionel Barrymore, and Gloria Grahame), and told with a sense of image and metaphor that appears in no other Capra film, IT'S A WONDERFUL LIFE is an epiphany of movie sentiment and a transcendent experience.
This 80th anniversary screening of IT'S A WONDERFUL LIFE is presented by Fathom Entertainment.
Directed by Frank Capra · PG

about: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris and Lee are dispatched from Santiago to Easter Island by their bureau chief, MJ. events.title: Being Heumann
about: By special arrangement with the film team, we are presenting BEING HEUMANN with additional accessibility options.
All screenings will be presented with Open Captions.
On Sunday 11/29, all screenings will be Sensory Friendly with sound at a lower volume and the lights not all the way lowered.

On Wednesday 12/2, all screenings will be presented with Open Audio Description, with the descriptive audio track usually available via special devices being played live through the theater's speaker system.

Scrappy, defiant, and done being treated like a burden, Judy Heumann turns her outrage into a revolution. In 1977, she and more than 100 disability rights protestors send a very loud message: The system is broken—not us.
Directed by Sian Heder · 2h 7m · R

events.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
about: Harry Lehman is an aging pickpocket who plies his trade with ever-diminishing returns in a drastically changed New York. Wallets stuffed with cash have been replaced by easily cancelled credit cards, and Harry struggles to make ends meet as he cares for his disabled wife, Rosie. When he unwittingly purloins and fences a valuable USB stick, Harry finds himself in a race against time to return the loot or face the rage of a vengeful crime family.
Directed by Noah Segan · 1h 28m · R

events.title: Sherlock Jr.
about: Witness some of the most mind-boggling stunts — and biggest laughs — in movie history when The Triplex screens Buster Keaton’s Sherlock, Jr. with a live score performed by Joanna Seaton and Donald Sosin on November 28th!

Joanna and Donnie have been accompanying silent films all over the world for many years, from MoMA and Lincoln Center to Telluride and Bologna, and from Bangkok to Berlin, and now they’re bringing their talents to The Triplex for a special screening presented in partnership with Christ Trinity Church of Sheffield to benefit Berkshire Bounty! Join us for a program that includes a singalong of songs from 1924, a slideshow of famous Sherlocks, an additional Buster Keaton short film, and Keaton’s iconic feature about a projectionist who dreams he’s a world famous detective.
Directed by Buster Keaton · 1h 20m · All Ages

events.title: The Green Knight
about: Q&A with costume designer Malgosia Turzanska!
We kick off the holiday season with The Green Knight, David Lowery’s stunning adaptation of the classic Arthurian legend, followed by a conversation with costume designer Malgosia Turzanska!

When the mythical Green Knight (Ralph Ineson) barges into King Arthur’s court on Christmas day, only Arthur’s headstrong nephew Sir Gawain (Dev Patel) accepts his challenge. Forced to face the knight the following Christmas, Gawain sets off on a journey filled with ghosts, giants, thieves, and schemers that tests his character and discover his true strength.

After the screening, we’ll be joined by Academy Award nominated costume designer Malgosia Turzanska to discuss the process of combining historical accuracy and fantasy elements to create the movie’s signature look, and what it took to bring her designs to life.
Directed by David Lowery · 2h 10m · R

events.title: Funk Night: Funksgiving
events.detail: with Beau Sasser, Jerry Cortez, Pete Antunes and Nate Fuller
about: GET YOUR FUNK NIGHT MERCH BEFORE THE SHOW SHOP FUNK NIGHT HERE🪩🎶 SHOW: 8:30pm / DOORS: 8:00pm Beau Sasser - Keys Featuring Jerry Cortez and Pete Antunes of Tower of Power Nate Fuller of Sax and Stache Beau Sasser has been a staple artist in the live music scene for decades. He is currently active throughout the Northeast and all over the country with the progressive funk/fusion band Kung Fu, the explosive Frank Zappa tribute band The Z3, the legendary New Orleans-grown Glen David Andrews Band, along with his own projects Escape Plan and Beau Sasser Trio - all of which allow his creative prowess over the keys and organ to shine.

Beau launched Funk Night in Northampton 18 years ago, and after taking the show on the road both far and wide, he's eager to bring his group of show-stopping friends along for the ride at the famed Iron Horse.

events.title: LuxDeluxe
about: The first thing you’ll notice about LuxDexlue is the singer, Ned King. He might be high-kicking, rolling on the floor, or squeezed up alongside drummer Jake Edwards with his own set of sticks in hand. Bassist Jacob Rosazza and rhythm guitarist Jake Manzi lean into their mics as Ned does, and 3-part Eagles-esque harmonies roll out. Then the energy shifts to stage left, where lead guitarist Caleb Rosazza has started soloing, and you know you’re in for a good night.

LuxDeluxe began in a poster-plastered basement in Northampton, Massachusetts in 2009. Three young cousins and two friends got together to play rock & roll, surrounded by stacks of records that included NRBQ, JJ Cale, and Tom Petty. The band rapidly gained recognition for their high-octane shows that left audiences sweaty and earned them the opportunity to share stages with Deer Tick, White Denim, Reptar, Lake Street Dive, Rubblebucket, J Mascis, NRBQ, and Big Al Anderson.

After a decade of writing, recording, and touring, a founding member of the band moved to LA to pursue film work. The pandemic closely followed. Like many bands during the events of 2020, LuxDeluxe went through a quiet period, during which they slowly built up a recording studio in an old warehouse building, and amassed a hoard of vintage guitars, keyboards, and amps. As guitarist Caleb Rosazza built up his inventory of recording gear, the rest of the band dug into honing their own skills, playing with other Western Mass bands, co-writing, and recording for other projects.

In 2022, the band re-convened to write and record over 100 songs, working and re-working to find their sound and identity again. And when they found themselves on stage for 2 sold-out New Year’s shows with NRBQ in 2023, something fell into place.

Their first new music in 7 years will be released in Fall 2024. This will be the band’s 6th release and 4th full-length album in the 15 years they have been together. The joy is still there. Evidence of time passing is, too. These aren’t the songs of kids barely out of high school any more. These songs bind the past to the present: the music may have evolved, but the heart and guts that make a LuxDeluxe record what it is shine through.

events.title: Ronnie Earl & The Broadcasters
about: Legendary Blues guitarist Ronnie Earl is a four-time Blues Music Award winner as Guitar Player of the Year (1997, 1999, 2014, 2018), most recently receiving the award on May 10, 2018, in Memphis. He has served as an Associate Professor of Guitar at Berklee College of Music and has taught at the National Guitar summer workshop in Connecticut.

In 1995 Ronnie released Ronnie Earl: Blues Guitar with Soul, an instructional VHS tape re-released in DVD format in 2005. Earl’s discography includes acclaimed albums on Stony Plain Records, Black Top, Bullseye Blues, Verve, and Telarc. His 1996 Bullseye Blues release, Grateful Heart: Blues and Ballads, won Downbeat Magazine’s Blues Album of the Year, and in 2004 Earl’s Hey José won the Best Blues/R&B Song at the 3rd Annual Independent Music Awards. In 2022, Ronnie Earl and the Broadcasters celebrate 35 years as a band. The recent releases by Ronnie Earl and the Broadcasters, Spread the Love (2010), Just for Today (2013), and Good News (2014), Father’s Day (2015), Maxwell Street (2016), and The Luckiest Man (2017), Beyond The Blue Door (2019) and Rise Up (2020) all debuted on the top ten Billboard Blues charts and received wide critical acclaim. Mercy Me (2022) is Earl’s 14th album in partnership with Stony Plain and his 28th career album.

events.title: Roomful of Blues
about: Roomful of Blues, the world-renowned, horn-powered, houserocking blues band, has been delighting audiences for over 55 years. Blues Music Magazine calls them “the best little big band in the blues.” On record and on stage, Roomful of Blues—led by master guitarist Chris Vachon for the past 25 years—continues to deliver its bone-shaking mix of original songs and carefully chosen covers ranging from jump, swing and proto rock ‘n’ roll to funky, contemporary blues. Their impeccable musicianship and larger-than-life vocals have earned Roomful of Blues five GRAMMY Award nominations and a slew of other accolades, including seven Blues Music Awards. Twice, the prestigious DownBeat International Critics’ Poll has selected them as Best Blues Band. And now, even after 18 previous releases and thousands of live shows, Roomful of Blues continues to evolve. Roomful of Blues, according to DownBeat magazine, “are in a class by themselves.” With their masterful combination of jumping, horn-heavy, hard-edged blues and R&B, it’s no wonder why the great Count Basie called them “the hottest blues band I’ve ever heard.” With a non-stop performance schedule for over 55 years, Roomful of Blues has earned critical, popular and radio success and a legion of fans around the globe. Roomful of Blues guitarist and bandleader Chris Vachon first joined in 1990 and has been leading the band since 1998. Guitar Player says Vachon’s guitar playing “burns with explosive solos and a delightfully greasy sense of rhythm.” The band has maintained its signature sound through great musicianship and a stellar horn section— featuring tenor and alto saxophonist Rich Lataille, who first joined the band in 1970. Lataille’s masterful playing can evoke either the fat-toned, honking sax of the glory days of early rock or the cool elegance of big band swing jazz.

Along with Vachon and Lataille, Roomful of Blues now includes new lead vocalist D.D. Bastos, new keyboardist Jeff Ceasrine, baritone and tenor saxophonist Craig Thomas, trumpeter Christopher Pratt, bassist Lou Bocciarelli and drummer Mike Coffey. The band has never sounded fresher or stronger, with Bastos bringing her sweet and soulful vocals and adding another bright new dimension to Roomful of Blues’ jazzy, jump-blues musical roots.
